MoSense raises RMB100-million-scale angel+ funding for robot touch

MoSkin, MoTact and MoWorld connect tactile structures, signal interpretation and decisions during physical contact.

PEdaily ↗26 October 2026English editorial summary
Story

Financing a complete touch stack

Shanghai-based MoSense, founded in May 2026, has raised angel+ financing described as RMB100-million-scale, co-led by CDH Investments and Oasis Capital. Participants include LimX Dynamics. The exact amount is undisclosed. Its approach spans electronic skin through action models.

Turning contact into useful signals

MoSkin uses deformable lattice structures to distribute loads. MoTact interprets multi-axis magnetic signals as force, displacement, slip and material information. The company describes 3D forming for curved surfaces and calibration methods intended to reduce integration work.

Tactile action models are still developing

MoWorld aims to combine touch with other modalities to revise actions during contact and narrow the simulation-to-reality gap. The report mentions robot-manufacturer collaborations without naming customers or providing independent benchmarks. Technical descriptions therefore do not establish factory durability or accuracy.
